fatal_errors: The hypothesis generalizes transformation-induced strengthening to other Mn-free quaternary and ternary alloys, whereas the cited evidence explicitly states that the FCC-to-HCP driving force was unique to CrCoNi and absent in the other equiatomic ternary derivatives.

It does not reconstruct the target's temperature-dependent single-crystal CRSS mechanism: MSAD-controlled solid-solution resistance, cryogenic inertial dulling, and high-temperature Cottrell-type Portevin–Le Chatelier pinning.
explanation: This is a testable and literature-supported alternative for the special case of CrCoNi: the quinary is an appropriate comparator, in situ/post-deformation TEM and XRD can detect HCP formation, and stress–strain measurements can test whether transformation correlates with hardening. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target study, which used [1̄23] single-crystal compression over 9–1373 K, strain-rate jumps, CRSS analysis, TEM, and DFT/MSAD correlations. Its tensile toughness and FCC-to-HCP predictions do not match the target outcomes. Evidence discipline is weakened substantially by extending a CrCoNi-specific result to Mn-free subsets generally, directly contrary to E2. The idea is also not novel relative to the cited paper, which already presents essentially the same mechanism.
